evidence_sources.citation: Erginkaya et al. (2025), A competitive disinhibitory network for robust optic flow processing in Drosophila
locators: Results: DNp15 is less sensitive to translational motion than HS; Fig.1
Results: DNp15's and bIPS' asymmetric activity drive steering; Fig.7b-d; Extended Data Fig.10a-d
Methods: Drosophila husbandry; exploratory walking arena; classification of walking paths
evidence_sources.target: DNp15 / DNHS1 neuron type, not exact MaleCNS specimen IDs
evidence_sources.preparation: Freely walking wing-clipped adults; circular heated-wall arena; tracked random-dot stimulus co-translates with fly; separate immobilized calcium imaging.
evidence_sources.behavioral_observable: Angular path deviation per forward distance during forward runs; saccade bias separately assessed.
evidence_sources.directional_result: Unilateral silencing/ablation biases paths contralaterally to the perturbed DNp15; bilateral/intact conditions show no systematic bias; saccades unaffected.
evidence_sources.applicability: Supports qualitative remaining-side course bias, not an identified transient bilateral activity-to-yaw transfer function.
limitations: No matched simultaneous bilateral activity/yaw transfer measurement
Chronic perturbation in a complete biological network
No physical gain, time constant or phase25 proxy calibration
Agent equations/fit are not biological measurements and are not adopted

evidence_sources.citation: Suver et al. (2016), An Array of Descending Visual Interneurons Encoding Self-Motion in Drosophila
evidence_sources.preparation: Tethered flight/quiescence; whole-cell recordings with motion stimuli and motor tracking
evidence_sources.applicability: Historical DNHS1 identity/visual response context; not the walking sign authority.
limitations: Flight readouts not free walking yaw
Correlation is not causal motor mapping
Spikes/voltage in biology do not add events/voltage semantics to Phase25 proxies

evidence_sources.citation: Pokusaeva et al. (2024), Bilateral interactions of optic-flow sensitive neurons coordinate course control in flies
evidence_sources.preparation: Free walking closed-loop visual stimulation; separate electrophysiology/dye coupling
evidence_sources.applicability: Electrical and stimulus/preparation context; not DNp15-specific yaw gain.
limitations: Nonlinear and stimulus-dependent behavior prevents treating HS motion descriptor as a measured body command

identity_compatibility.basis: Published DNp15/DNHS1 correspondence and bilateral type; pinned right 11215/left 12069 metadata.

directional_evidence.proposed_model_relation: Higher right proxy relative to left maps to positive rightward model orientation; reverse imbalance maps leftward.
directional_evidence.negative_proxy_interpretation: Exploratory model extension only; not negative firing rate or measured reverse-direction motor physiology.

preparation_compatibility.target_observable_not: Tethered wing steering, head yaw alone, rapid saccade command, or calibrated free-flight yaw
limits: Walking trajectory curvature is not a time-resolved instantaneous yaw law
Phase25 50 ms is not the biological assay horizon
No freely moving biological yaw predicted

stage_a.reason: Type-compatible causal directional perturbations justify an explicitly assumed signed orientation abstraction; magnitude and dynamics remain uncalibrated.

allowed_claims: No biological amplitude or timing calibration
